newsitem.title: UK: ASDA can help on UK govt jobs scheme - ceo.
newsitem.headline: ASDA can help on UK govt jobs scheme - ceo.

text.p: Allan Leighton, chief executive of British supermarket group ASDA Plc, said on Thursday he was "sure we will be able to help" the new Labour government in its plans for new deal to combat youth unemployment.
Leighton, who attended a working breakfast for more than 40 company chiefs with Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Wednesday, said he was "very impressed".
"They were very professional, very listening and keen to work with us and I...was very encouraged by that," Leighton said.

The "welfare-to-work" scheme, which will use three billion pounds raised from a one-off tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities, will be the central plank of the government's first budget on July 2.
Brown needs companies to sign up to the scheme, which offers state subsidies to firms willing to take on young unemployed people for six months of work experience and training.
"There's a germ of a very good idea here," he said.
Leighton said companies were keen to "help them develop a programme which is enduring, rather than something that just lasts for six months".
